posts.body:
Hi.
I'm trying to make a character profile page for the game I'm working on but I don't know how to pull up variables and stuff for how I envisioned it. I will make for each character a background image that will have all the characters, window borders, and text boxes drawn out and as much text filled out as possible. The only thing I would need to fill in is the profile page and game_variables which should be pulled from the game.
I don't think you could do that through an editor but maybe you can I just don't know what script calls to make.
What I made so far is this:
When a player uses an item, a common event is called and the player selects which character's profile page he wants to open. Based on his selection, a profile image for that character is displayed (through show picture) and information stored in game_variables should be displayed or x character.
This is the part where I'm having trouble. I don't know how to make a script call to pull out a variable value and display it in x,y position. This needs to be done for all other variables. And when a player closes the image, I need to be able to clear all the variables as well.
Am I going about this the wrong way? My knowledge of scripting is very limited. I can edit an already existing script, but to make my own is impossible. This was the only way I could think of doing this.
Does anyone know any scripts I could maybe use/edit to make something like this?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
most of the game values you can get through control variable : game data (which is much more than just the map ID).
you can place variables inside show text to display them, and with message type plugins and gab window plugins you can move and resize the show text however you want.
and you can place text into any variable by placing a string with "string"  into the script box of control variable, it will be automatically displayed as text inside the show text.

Ruby:
#==============================================================================
# ** Scene_CharacterProfile
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This scene shows the character profile including actor information and image.
#==============================================================================
class Scene_CharacterProfile < Scene_Base
  # Initialize the scene with the actor's ID from game variable 221
  def initialize
    @actor_id = $game_variables[221]
  end

  # Start the scene
  def start
    super
    create_background
    create_actor_info
  end

  # Create the background
  def create_background
    @background_sprite = Sprite.new
    @background_sprite.bitmap = Cache.picture("Profile_Background")
  end

  # Create the actor information display
  def create_actor_info
    @actor = $game_actors[@actor_id]
    if @actor.nil?
      msgbox("Actor with ID #{@actor_id} does not exist.")
      $scene = Scene_Map.new
      return
    end

    # Create and position the character image
    @character_sprite = Sprite.new
    begin
      @character_sprite.bitmap = Cache.picture("actor_#{@actor_id}")
    rescue
      msgbox("Image for actor ID #{@actor_id} not found.")
      $scene = Scene_Map.new
      return
    end
    @character_sprite.x = 0
    @character_sprite.y = 0

    # Create the information window with the specified size
    @info_window = Window_Base.new(0, 0, 544, 416)
    update_info_window
  end

  # Update the information window with the actor's data
  def update_info_window
    @info_window.contents.clear
    @info_window.contents.draw_text(0, 0, 544, 32, "Name: #{@actor.name}")
    @info_window.contents.draw_text(0, 32, 544, 32, "Class: #{@actor.class.name}")
    @info_window.contents.draw_text(0, 64, 544, 32, "Level: #{@actor.level}")
    # Add additional actor information based on game variables
    @info_window.contents.draw_text(0, 96, 544, 32, "HP: #{$game_variables[1]}")
    @info_window.contents.draw_text(0, 128, 544, 32, "MP: #{$game_variables[2]}")
  end

  # Terminate the scene
  def terminate
    super
    dispose_background
    dispose_actor_info
  end

  # Dispose of the background
  def dispose_background
    @background_sprite.bitmap.dispose
    @background_sprite.dispose
  end

  # Dispose of the actor information display
  def dispose_actor_info
    @character_sprite.bitmap.dispose if @character_sprite.bitmap
    @character_sprite.dispose
    @info_window.dispose
  end

  # Update the scene
  def update
    super
    update_actor_selection if Input.trigger?(Input::LEFT) || Input.trigger?(Input::RIGHT)
    if Input.trigger?(Input::B) # Return to the previous scene when the B button is pressed
      Sound.play_cancel
      $scene = Scene_Map.new
    end
  end

  # Update actor selection based on input
  def update_actor_selection
    if Input.trigger?(Input::LEFT)
      previous_actor
    elsif Input.trigger?(Input::RIGHT)
      next_actor
    end
    update_info_window
    update_character_image
  end

  # Select the previous actor
  def previous_actor
    loop do
      @actor_id = (@actor_id - 1)
      @actor_id = 10 if @actor_id < 1
      break if $game_actors[@actor_id] && $game_switches[600 + @actor_id]
    end
    @actor = $game_actors[@actor_id]
  end

  # Select the next actor
  def next_actor
    loop do
      @actor_id = (@actor_id + 1) % 11
      @actor_id = 1 if @actor_id == 0
      break if $game_actors[@actor_id] && $game_switches[600 + @actor_id]
    end
    @actor = $game_actors[@actor_id]
  end

  # Update the character image
  def update_character_image
    @character_sprite.bitmap.dispose if @character_sprite.bitmap
    @character_sprite.bitmap = Cache.picture("actor_#{@actor_id}")
  end
end

# Script call to open the character profile page
def open_character_profile
  $scene = Scene_CharacterProfile.new
end

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
kR1pt0n1t3 said:
you can use ChatGPT to make scripts for RPG Maker and I just tried and it's insane how good it works.
Click to expand...
No, it doesn't work at all - you just have been very lucky with the randomiser inside the AI.
What all AIs do is compile a list of existing parts created by real programmers (or artists or musicians ...) tagged witrh keywords of what they do, then ran your keywords against the list of keywords they have and randomly select one of the code that has fitting keywords before running it through a syntax check and so on.
if there are enough preexisting scripts that do what you want and if you know how to pinpoint keywords, then you have a good chance of getting something working.
but since it's copied from existing scripts/plugins you are mostly still better off looking for the  original.
If you want something that was never done before or if you have no idea how to describe what you want, the results of any AI are absolute crap, and the programmers of this forum have long grown tired of trying to fix those randomized jumbles of pseudo-script.
As someone once said - it is only a question of time until an alphanumeric randomizer recreates shakespeare's complete works - a question of very, very long time...
